title: Edinburgh Hogmanay 2027: Street Party tickets and New Year’s Day
description: Plan Edinburgh Hogmanay 2026–2027: the confirmed 31 December Street Party, tickets and ages, transport still pending and New Year’s Day opening.
intro: To celebrate Hogmanay and welcome 2027 in Edinburgh, distinguish the street celebration from other concerts and New Year’s Day visits. The organiser’s specific event page confirms the Street Party on 31 December 2026 at 8 pm, on Princes Street, with its own ticket and a 12+ age restriction. Staying in a central hotel does not itself admit you. This guide organises that evening and two daytime additions: Edinburgh Castle and the National Museum of Scotland.

The 12 November 2026 review found information updated to different stages. The Street Party has a dated page and programme, while the general About body retains pending-programme wording and references to the previous New Year. Lothian still displays 2025–2026 festive timetables. Specific event pages therefore establish the celebration, attraction operators establish holiday visits, and special transport and some New Year’s Day festival activities remain points to verify.

sections.heading: Princes Street: the party location and its own admission
paragraphs: The official page places the Street Party on Princes Street and dates its start to 8 pm on 31 December 2026. It publishes acts and specific areas, including a Sophie Ellis-Bextor and Richard Jones DJ set on the Waverley Bridge stage. That detail belongs to this edition’s event page rather than a list of past performers. When comparing tickets, verify the event name: the Gardens concert and activities on other nights are not automatically part of the same admission.

Organise entry using your ticket instructions and final operational map rather than an ordinary daytime walk along the street. The documentary photograph shows Princes Street with traffic in 2010; it identifies the urban setting, not Hogmanay 2026 gates, stages or circulation. The organiser warns that only its official channels and named sellers issue valid tickets, with no official resale. Keep your 2026–2027 electronic ticket accessible so you can retrieve it on arrival.

sections.heading: Edinburgh Castle: a daytime visit with a later 1 January start
paragraphs: The castle can give substance to the preceding day or New Year’s Day, but it must not be confused with admission to the festival arena. Its operator lists 9:30 am opening from 27 to 31 December, closing at 5 pm with last admission at 4 pm. On 1 January, opening moves to 11 am while the other two times remain. Planning a normal early morning visit could leave you waiting outside an entrance that has not opened.

The operator recommends at least two hours for the main attractions and warns that once online tickets sell out, there are no further admissions held back at the gate. Choose a slot compatible with your rest after the party. Internal museums and spaces have their own exceptions, so castle opening does not mean every part is available. The photograph records the esplanade in 2021; it establishes no public castle access during midnight fireworks operations or guaranteed position from which to see them.

sections.heading: National Museum of Scotland: a New Year’s Day option from noon
paragraphs: The National Museum of Scotland on Chambers Street publishes 1 January opening from noon to 5 pm rather than its usual daily hours. That allows an afternoon cultural visit without requiring an early start after Hogmanay. Its programme includes Roman Scotland: Life on the Edge of Empire from 14 November 2026 to 18 April 2027, spanning the change of year. Choose according to your interests and check the exhibition’s specific admission conditions.

General admission is free, while some exhibitions have separate charges. Museum visitor information includes lifts and ramps for galleries and exhibitions, alongside other accessibility resources. Check the details you need before choosing a route and the conditions for any special exhibition. Building admission and festival events remain independent. If you combine museum and castle on the same day, respect their admission windows and the change in elevation. After a long night, choosing just one can leave more space for food and rest instead of spending the afternoon racing between entrances.

sections.heading: The 2026–2027 calendar: specific announcements versus generic pages
paragraphs: Forever Edinburgh, the city tourism website, announces the festival from 29 December 2026 to 1 January 2027. For the Street Party, the organiser’s individual page supplies a specific date, start, location, age restriction and programme. That information is more useful than a generic About sentence still saying 2026 tickets are coming soon. The inconsistency does not require dismissing the whole website; it requires checking which text corresponds to the exact event and year you are booking.

For New Year’s Day, the About body also recalls First Footin’ activities from 2026. Those names, venues and times are not presented here as a complete 2027 programme. If a festival activity interests you that afternoon, consult its dated page when available. Meanwhile, the castle and museum provide visits with checked holiday arrangements. Your break need not depend on filling the diary with last year’s events or assuming a performance is confirmed because it appears in a photo gallery.

sections.heading: Tickets and ages: choose the event that actually suits your group
paragraphs: The Street Party and Gardens concert are different products. The FAQ specifies electronic tickets for 2026–2027 and no readmission for both celebrations: leaving means you cannot return on the same ticket. That affects a dinner booked outside the arena or plans to drop belongings at the hotel halfway through the night. Check the event, date, allocated entrance and conditions before paying rather than relying on the word Hogmanay alone.

The organiser marks the Street Party, Gardens and Night Afore as 12+, and requires under 16s to hold full-price tickets and attend with an adult over 18. Family events can have different rules; an activity intended for children does not automatically admit them to the evening party. For visitors needing personal assistance or mobility arrangements, the FAQ describes separate procedures and limited accessible viewing places. Checking with the organiser before buying is more useful than assuming any ticket resolves access.

sections.heading: Prepare for an outdoor night and a workable journey back
paragraphs: The FAQ describes entry searches, bag and item restrictions and a no-umbrellas rule, alongside differences between arenas. Choose clothing suitable for remaining outdoors and review the forecast before setting out. Do not transfer the Street Party’s drink rules to the Gardens concert: the organiser lists them separately. Agree a meeting place outside the area that does not depend on one entrance, and arrange food within the rules of your chosen event.

For the journey back, the Lothian festive page checked here still supplies 2025–2026 information and previous Hogmanay links. It does not establish overnight buses, fares or the morning service on 1 January 2027. Wait for the 2026–2027 plan, then check diversions and the route from your exit gate. With an early flight or train, calculate your margin using the service actually available rather than relying on free travel or routes from a previous edition.

itinerary: 30 December or arrival day: settle in, review tickets and orient yourself around the event area in daylight, recognising that entrances may change. If you want a castle visit before the main evening, reserve that block and check which internal areas are open. Another separately ticketed party is not essential simply to fill a multi-day calendar.

31 December: a lighter morning, a meal at a compatible time, rest and preparation for the party. Its event page advertises an 8 pm start; verify the entry instructions attached to your admission. Carry permitted belongings and remember that leaving does not allow readmission. Have the journey back arranged before the countdown.

1 January: allow a later start. The castle lists 11 am opening and the museum noon; the rest of the festival does not automatically share their availability. One visit and an unhurried meal may be enough. For other days, the general Edinburgh and Christmas guides linked below add possibilities without recycling their dates as the 2027 Hogmanay programme.

faq.question: Which night welcomes 2027 at Edinburgh Hogmanay?
faq.answer: The main evening is 31 December 2026. City tourism dates the festival from 29 December to 1 January, and the Street Party page confirms an 8 pm start on 31 December on Princes Street.

faq.question: Is the Edinburgh Street Party free?
faq.answer: No. The organiser sells a specific electronic admission for 2026–2027. Do not confuse it with free activities that may take place on another festival day or ordinary daytime access to Princes Street.

faq.question: Can children enter the Street Party?
faq.answer: The event page and FAQ specify ages 12 and over. Under 16s need a full-price ticket and an accompanying adult over 18. Check the particular event rules, because family activities have different conditions.

faq.question: What can I visit in Edinburgh on 1 January?
faq.answer: Operator pages list the castle from 11 am to 5 pm, with last admission at 4 pm, and the National Museum of Scotland from noon to 5 pm. Review possible changes and choose a visit that fits your rest after the celebration.

faq.question: Are the 2026–2027 Hogmanay special buses confirmed?
faq.answer: The Lothian festive page captured for this review still covers 2025–2026. Its intervals and fares are not repeated for 2027. Consult the current-season update and operational notices before travelling.

conclusion: Hogmanay works better with a specific celebration, the correct ticket and a realistic start to the following day. Princes Street anchors this evening; castle and museum provide daytime visits with checked holiday opening. Distinguishing dated programmes, older copy and pending transport helps you book with more confidence and enjoy the change of year without relying on assumptions.
